request.system:
You draft incident communications for Hartwell's
HR shared-services team. Use only the facts given. Write two
parts, each under its heading:
NOTICE: a plain notice to each affected employee, under 150
words, from the HR Shared Services team.
SUMMARY: one paragraph, under 120 words, for the incident
record a regulator or auditor may read.
A person will check and send them; you send nothing.

messages.content:
Facts:
- On Tuesday, November 16, 2027 at 6:10 p.m. Denver time, Hartwell's evening feed to its US payroll provider sent the same batch of approved changes twice after a timeout.
- 37 employees had a bank-detail change in that batch. The provider recorded each of their changes twice and, under its own fraud rule for two changes within 24 hours, put the new deposit account on hold.
- Every account was the account the employee had asked for. No account details went to anyone who should not have them, and no money moved to a wrong account.
- While on hold, the next pay would have gone by paper check instead of direct deposit.
- Each of the 37 received two emails from the provider saying their direct deposit had changed.
- Hartwell's payroll readback found the problem at 5:42 a.m. on Wednesday, November 17. All 37 holds were released and read back by 8:02 p.m. that day.
- Pay on Friday, November 19, 2027 goes by direct deposit to the new account as normal. Employees need to do nothing.
- Questions go to AskHartwell or the HR service line; an adviser can confirm the account on file.
- The feed's automatic retry has been switched off and will come back only with a check that stops a batch being sent twice.

content.text:
**NOTICE**

Subject: Your direct deposit change: no action needed

Dear employee,

On November 16, 2027, a file of approved payroll changes was sent to our US payroll provider twice. Your bank-detail change was in that file, so the provider recorded it twice and placed your new deposit account on hold. Without a fix, your next pay could have gone by paper check.

You may have received two emails from the provider saying your direct deposit had changed. This came from the duplicate file, not from any new request by you.

The account on hold is the one you asked for. No one else received your account details, and no money went to a wrong account. We released all holds on November 17.

Your November 19 pay will go by direct deposit to your new account, as normal. You do not need to do anything.

Questions? Contact AskHartwell or the HR service line. An adviser can confirm the account on file for you.

HR Shared Services

**SUMMARY**

On November 16, 2027 at 6:10 p.m. Denver time, a timeout caused Hartwell's evening payroll feed to send a batch twice to its US provider. The provider recorded 37 employees' bank-detail changes twice and, under its fraud rule, held each new deposit account. Every account was the one requested; no details reached unauthorized parties and no funds went to a wrong account. Without correction, the next pay would have issued by paper check. Payroll readback detected the issue at 5:42 a.m. November 17; all holds were released and verified by 8:02 p.m. November 17. November 19 pay proceeds by direct deposit. Automatic retry is disabled pending a control that prevents duplicate batches.

**NOTICE**

Subject: Your direct deposit change: no action needed

Dear [Employee name],

On Tuesday, November 16, 2027, a data transfer from Hartwell to our US payroll provider sent your bank-detail change twice. As a result, the provider placed a temporary hold on your new deposit account. You may have received two emails from the provider saying your direct deposit had changed. Both came from this same error.

We found the problem on the morning of November 17 and released the hold that day. Your new account is the one you requested. No account details were shared with anyone who should not have them, and no money went to a wrong account.

Your pay on Friday, November 19, 2027 will go by direct deposit to your new account as normal. You do not need to do anything.

If you have questions, contact AskHartwell or the HR service line. An HR adviser can confirm the account on file for you.

HR Shared Services
Hartwell

**SUMMARY**

On November 16, 2027, at 6:10 p.m. Denver time, Hartwell's evening payroll feed to its US provider resent an approved change batch after a timeout. Thirty-seven bank-detail changes were recorded twice. Under the provider's two-changes-in-24-hours rule, it placed the new deposit accounts on hold. Each affected employee received two provider notices of a direct deposit change. Hartwell's payroll readback detected the issue at 5:42 a.m. on November 17; all holds were released and verified by 8:02 p.m. that day. Every account was the one requested. No details reached unauthorized parties, and no funds went to wrong accounts. Otherwise, the next pay would have gone by paper check. The feed's automatic retry is disabled until a control preventing duplicate sends is in place.
